_comment: For projects bootstrapped BEFORE the hardened PostToolUse hook was introduced. The installer will not overwrite an existing .claude/settings.local.json (neither the default install nor --update touch the `hooks` block), so existing projects must apply this upgrade manually. Replace the `command` value of the PostToolUse hook whose matcher is "Edit|Write" in your project's .claude/settings.local.json with the `replacement_command` string below. This upgrades the naive design (validates on every Edit/Write, no file filter, no debounce, no auto-sync) — the source of false-block noise on unrelated file edits and on rapid mirror edits across BACKLOG.md/TASK_STATUS.md — to the hardened design mavericks itself uses.
protections: File-path filter — the hook exits 0 immediately unless the edited file path ends in BACKLOG.md or TASK_STATUS.md. File-path extraction reads the hook payload JSON from stdin using `node -e` (NOT python3 — node is already a hard dependency, python3 may be absent in some environments).

Debounce — a gitignored timestamp file (.mavp-hook-ts) at the project root ensures that when multiple BACKLOG.md/TASK_STATUS.md edits land in the same turn, only the LAST one runs the validator; earlier invocations detect they have been superseded and exit 0 silently before validating.

Auto-sync — on a BACKLOG.md edit, mavp-operator-sync-status.js runs BEFORE the validator, mirroring Active Wave statuses into TASK_STATUS.md first. This is the essential fix for mirror-edit false blocks: debounce alone only reduces noise volume, it does not resolve a genuinely transient BACKLOG/TASK_STATUS mismatch mid-edit.

Advisory exit-0 — the hook always exits 0. Validator output, when the validator itself reports drift (exit code 1) or requires repair (exit code 2), is printed to stderr only — it never blocks the Edit/Write tool call.
replacement_command: INPUT=$(cat); FP=$(node -e "try{const d=JSON.parse(require('fs').readFileSync(0,'utf8'));process.stdout.write((d.tool_input&&d.tool_input.file_path)||'')}catch(e){}" <<< "$INPUT"); case "$FP" in *BACKLOG.md|*TASK_STATUS.md) ;; *) exit 0 ;; esac; MAVERICKS="${MAVERICKS_HOME:-$( [ -d "$HOME/.mavericks" ] && printf %s "$HOME/.mavericks" || printf %s "$HOME/Documents/mavericks" )}/scripts"; MAVROOT="__PROJECT_ROOT__"; export MAVERICKS_PROJECT_ROOT="$MAVROOT"; TS=$(node -e "process.stdout.write(String(Date.now()))"); echo "$TS" > "$MAVROOT/.mavp-hook-ts"; sleep 1.5; CURRENT_TS=$(cat "$MAVROOT/.mavp-hook-ts" 2>/dev/null); if [ "$CURRENT_TS" != "$TS" ]; then exit 0; fi; rm -f "$MAVROOT/.mavp-hook-ts"; cd "$MAVROOT"; case "$FP" in *BACKLOG.md) node "$MAVERICKS/mavp-operator-sync-status.js" 1>&2 ;; esac; VOUT=$(node "$MAVERICKS/mavp-validator.js" 2>&1); VCODE=$?; [ $VCODE -ne 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "$VOUT" >&2 || true; exit 0
migration_steps: Replace __PROJECT_ROOT__ in replacement_command with your project's absolute root path (the directory containing your scripts/mavp-operator).
Add `.mavp-hook-ts` to your project's .gitignore — the debounce timestamp file must never be committed.

If your project has already adopted templates/doc-sync-hook.fragment.json, keep its `case "$FP" in *TASK_STATUS.md) ...` fragment appended after the validator step (before the final `exit 0`) — it is compatible with this hardened base.

Resolution order for MAVERICKS: explicit MAVERICKS_HOME env var > ~/.mavericks (canonical) > ~/Documents/mavericks (legacy fallback). Set MAVERICKS_HOME if your mavericks installation lives somewhere else entirely.

MAVERICKS_PROJECT_ROOT is exported so mavp-operator-sync-status.js (which resolves its target root from that env var, not process.cwd()) operates on YOUR project's BACKLOG.md/TASK_STATUS.md rather than the mavericks framework checkout — required because the framework scripts are referenced out-of-tree.
requires: Node.js (already a hard dependency); no python3 dependency; scripts/mavp-operator-sync-status.js and scripts/mavp-validator.js available from the mavericks installation
